text: Confirm it directly, as the account that actually matters here: `sudo -u orderapi sh -c 'echo test >> /var/log/orderapi/orderapi.log'`. Permission denied -- but the file has plenty of old content in it, so `orderapi` clearly used to be able to write to it.

Look at the file itself: `ls -l /var/log/orderapi/orderapi.log`. It's owned by `root:root` with mode `0600` -- not `orderapi`. Now check what logrotate was told to do: `cat /etc/logrotate.d/orderapi`.

The `create 0600 root root` line is the problem. That directive tells logrotate exactly what owner/mode to stamp on the fresh file it creates right after each rotation -- and it's set to the wrong user entirely. It needs to match the account the service actually runs as.

Fix it: `sudo sed -i 's/create 0600 root root/create 0640 orderapi orderapi/' /etc/logrotate.d/orderapi`. Then force a rotation to prove it end-to-end: `sudo rm -f /var/log/orderapi/orderapi.log.1 /var/lib/logrotate/status && sudo logrotate --force /etc/logrotate.d/orderapi`, and confirm `sudo -u orderapi sh -c 'echo test >> /var/log/orderapi/orderapi.log'` now succeeds.
